skill.name: lark-openapi-explorer
skill.description: Explore official Feishu and Lark OpenAPI documentation when existing Lark skills or CLI commands do not cover a user request.
skill.summary: Find native Lark OpenAPI endpoints and prepare safe lark-cli api calls from official documentation.
skill.author: larksuite

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are markdown false positives from code fences, inline code, official documentation URLs, and sibling skill links. The real residual risk is intentional lark-cli usage for authenticated Lark OpenAPI calls, including mutating POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE operations that require explicit user confirmation.

remediation.issue: Authenticated lark-cli API calls can change tenant data.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the existing confirmation requirement for POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE operations, and show the method, path, parameters, and expected impact before execution.

remediation.issue: Raw API paths and parameters are assembled from documentation and user goals.
remediation.suggestion: Require every path, method, and parameter to be copied from official documentation rather than inferred, and prefer dry-run previews when supported.

remediation.issue: The skill fetches external documentation from Feishu and Lark domains.
remediation.suggestion: Limit WebFetch usage to the documented official OpenAPI domains and do not send tenant secrets or private records in documentation lookup prompts.

content.value_statement: Lark and Feishu tasks sometimes need APIs that are not wrapped by existing skills or CLI commands. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through official documentation to find the right endpoint and prepare safe CLI calls.
actual_capabilities: Checks whether an existing Lark skill or CLI command already covers the user request.
Fetches official Feishu or Lark OpenAPI index pages to locate relevant modules.
Finds specific API documentation pages for unsupported Lark operations.
Extracts methods, paths, parameters, permissions, responses, and error details from official docs.
Prepares lark-cli api command examples for GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE requests.
Requires confirmation before write or delete style API calls.
limitations: Requires lark-cli to be installed and authenticated before API calls can run.
Depends on official Feishu or Lark documentation being reachable and current.
Does not replace tenant permissions, app approval, or admin consent requirements.
Can identify unsupported APIs, but it cannot guarantee that every API is enabled for a tenant.

use_cases.title: Find an unsupported chat API
use_cases.description: Locate the official OpenAPI endpoint when a chat management task is not covered by existing CLI commands.

use_cases.title: Prepare safe API calls
use_cases.description: Turn official documentation into a reviewed lark-cli api call with method, path, parameters, scopes, and cautions.

use_cases.title: Document native API options
use_cases.description: Summarize available OpenAPI capabilities for a product or operations workflow before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Check if an API is needed
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether an existing Lark skill or lark-cli command can handle my request: add members to a chat. If not, find the official OpenAPI path.

prompt_templates.title: Find a specific endpoint
prompt_templates.scenario: Locate an endpoint from official documentation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Lark OpenAPI documentation to find the endpoint for updating a chat announcement. Return the method, path, required scopes, and key parameters.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a reviewed CLI call
prompt_templates.scenario: Convert documentation into an executable plan.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the official API for adding users to a chat, then prepare the lark-cli api call. Ask for confirmation before any write operation.

prompt_templates.title: Compare API options for a workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Research official Lark APIs needed to create a chat, add members, and set an announcement. Summarize the sequence, permissions, risks, and confirmation points.

output_examples.input: Find how to add members to a Lark chat when the CLI has no direct command.
output_examples.output: The skill reports that no wrapped command was found, identifies the official chat member endpoint, lists required member identifiers and permissions, and asks for confirmation before the POST call.

output_examples.input: I need to update a group announcement through Lark OpenAPI.
output_examples.output: The skill returns the official announcement update endpoint, explains required fields such as revision and content requests, and highlights that the operation changes visible chat content.

output_examples.input: Document the API options for a workflow that manages chats.
output: Separates safe read steps from write steps that need confirmation.

best_practices: Start by checking existing Lark skills and CLI commands before exploring raw OpenAPI calls.
Use only official Feishu or Lark documentation as the source for paths, parameters, and permissions.
Review the full request and business impact before approving write or delete operations.
anti_patterns: Do not guess API paths, request bodies, or permission scopes from memory.
Do not run mutating API calls without an explicit user confirmation step.
Do not include tenant secrets or private user data in documentation search prompts.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when a Lark or Feishu task is not covered by an existing skill or registered lark-cli command.

faq.question: Does it execute API calls automatically?
faq.answer: It can prepare lark-cli api calls, but write and delete operations should require user confirmation before execution.

faq.question: Which documentation sources does it use?
faq.answer: It uses official Feishu and Lark OpenAPI documentation indexes and API pages.

faq.question: Can it work in English?
faq.answer: Yes. The source documentation is Chinese, but the skill instructs the assistant to translate results when the user uses English.

faq.question: What tools are required?
faq.answer: The skill requires lark-cli for API calls and WebFetch for official documentation lookup.

faq.question: Can it bypass Lark permissions?
faq.answer: No. API calls still require valid authentication, app scopes, tenant permissions, and any required approvals.
